load_basis: Annual average draw, not peak and not IT capacity: 1,674,619 MWh reported by Meta in its annual data center report to the Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment, as published by KOLN on 2026-10-29, divided by 8,760 hours. The article does not state the reporting year; it is taken to be calendar 2025 because the MARA figure in the same table equals NPPD's posted 2025 figure. Peak demand was not reported.
notes: Meta's own Environmental Data Index gives facility electricity use of 5,000 MWh (2018), 178,000 (2019), 519,000 (2020), 736,810 (2021), 1,007,635 (2022), 1,148,091 (2023) and 1,258,239 MWh (2024; 143.2 average MW) - see https://sustainability.atmeta.com/asset/2025-environmental-data-index. First meaningful load is therefore 2019. Service: Meta's info sheet says it worked with OPPD to plan its energy needs; OPPD created a dedicated large-load service schedule in 2017 that Facebook signed onto (customer owns its substation, transmission-voltage service) per https://www.gov1.com/energy/articles/how-public-power-is-growing-the-silicon-prairie-fATZm5PukPMze4cI/ - classed here as special_contract although it is a published schedule, not a bilateral contract. The inventory holds five records for this campus: osm:way/844394340, osm:way/1253282100, osm:way/1253282101, osm:way/1253282102 and epoch:Meta Sarpy (2026 start, 80 MW). The 191.2 MW here is the whole campus, so it must not be added to the Epoch record. Coordinates are the OSM building centroid already in the inventory. No full-buildout MW found in a citable source.

site_name: Google Papillion data center campus (Fireball Group LLC)
load_basis: Peak electric demand (not average, not IT capacity) reported by Google in its annual data center report to the Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment, as published by KOLN on 2026-10-29. Reporting year not stated in the article; taken to be calendar 2025.
notes: Published address is 14706 Schram Road, Papillion (KMTV); coordinates are the OSM building centroid already in the inventory (osm:way/1237494981), not geocoded from the address. Other inventory records on this campus: osm:way/1237494981 and osm:way/1312801354. Year: Sarpy County's 2021 annual report (published 2021-12-20) says Google's first Papillion data center was already operational; Google announced the site in October 2019 with an 18-24 month build. First operation could be 2020 or 2021, hence medium confidence; the inventory's 2023 start looks late. Service arrangement not found in a citable source (OPPD has a dedicated large-load schedule and a separate Google transaction for the Pierce County solar and battery project, https://oppdthewire.com/oppd-google-join-forces-with-nextera-on-solar-and-battery-project/). Cross-check: OPPD industrial sales rose from 3,371,856 MWh (2018) to 6,927,893 MWh (2025) per https://oppd.com/media/321483/2025-statistics.pdf; after subtracting Meta's 1,674,619 MWh, roughly 1.9 TWh (about 215 average MW) is left for the two Google OPPD campuses plus all other industrial growth. That residual is my own arithmetic, not a reported figure.

site_name: Google Omaha data center campus (Westwood Solutions LLC)
load_basis: Peak electric demand (not average, not IT capacity) reported by Google in its annual data center report to the Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment, as published by KOLN on 2026-10-29. Reporting year not stated in the article; taken to be calendar 2025.
notes: Northwest Omaha, near State Street and Blair High Road (KMTV, April 2022). Flatwater Free Press (2026-03-13) says the roughly 260-acre site was announced in 2022 and began operating in 2024 while construction continued. Coordinates are the OSM building centroid already in the inventory; other records on this campus: osm:way/1422101108, osm:way/1422101112, osm:way/1422101116. Utility: the cited article treats Google's Omaha-region load as OPPD load; no source names the service arrangement. The inventory's 237 MW for this campus is well above the 98.32 MW peak Google reported to the state.

load_basis: Peak electrical demand reported by Agate LLC in its annual data center report to the Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment, recovered by KOLN from improperly redacted filings (2026-09-30). Usage figures in the filings appear to cover 2025. Peak, not average: the site was only commissioning in late 2025, so its 2025 average load was far lower.
notes: North Lincoln near I-80 and North 56th Street / Highway 77; no street address published, so lat/lon left null (the inventory record already carries 40.9060, -96.6533, which I did not verify). Sources conflict on the start year: KOLN (2025-05-05) said LES expected it in service in fall 2025 and a 2025 peak demand was reported to the state, but Google's own Nebraska page lists Lincoln as coming online in 2026 (https://datacenters.google/locations/nebraska/). I used 2025 at medium confidence. LES says it has an agreement with Google for a facility in excess of 20 MW and buys the energy from the Southwest Power Pool; Google paid for its substations (https://siliconprairienews.com/2025/11/nebraska-can-take-lessons-from-virginias-data-center-boom-to-prep-its-power-grids/). The inventory's 141 MW is well above the 52.65 MW reported peak. A separate, much larger Google proposal in southeast Nebraska (1,000-3,000 MW, possibly 2029) is not this site.

site_name: MARA Kearney (former Compute North NE01), Tech oNE Crossing
load_basis: 2025 annual average draw: 786,878,934 kWh posted by NPPD for its 'Operation 1' under the LB 526 cryptocurrency disclosure, divided by 8,760 hours. NPPD does not name the operation; it is matched to this site because MARA reported the same 786,878 MWh and a 99 MW peak in its state annual report (https://www.1011now.com/2026/10/29/data-centers-decoded-water-electricity-usage-put-into-context/).
notes: Open-air bitcoin mine on about 11 acres in Kearney's Tech oNE Crossing park. Compute North announced it live on 2019-11-21; it was 30 MW in March 2021 and expanded to 100 MW that year. Ownership went Compute North (bankrupt 2022) to Generate Capital to Marathon/MARA. NPPD serves Kearney at retail; the load is interruptible, and NPPD built a substation that Compute North paid for. Reported peak 99 MW. WOWT (2026-09-08) reports MARA plans to hand its 100 MW to a proposed 368 MW data center campus (Tech One Crossing, first phase late 2027), which is a future project and not counted here. Coordinates are the OSM centroid already in the inventory.

site_name: Southern Public Power District cryptocurrency mining Site 1 (operator and location not disclosed)
serving_utility: Southern Public Power District (wholesale customer of NPPD)
load_basis: Annual average draw: 261,184 MWh posted by Southern Public Power District for 'Site 1' under the LB 526 cryptocurrency disclosure, labeled 'as of December 2025', divided by 8,760 hours. Assumes the figure is a full calendar year.
notes: Southern's page lists three crypto sites without names or locations: Site 1 261,184 MWh, Site 2 39,697 MWh (about 4.5 average MW), Site 3 23,490 MWh (about 2.7 average MW). Sites 2 and 3 are under 10 MW and not given their own rows. Southern's territory covers south-central Nebraska including the Minden, Aurora and rural Grand Island areas. Named crypto operations known there: Foundry Digital in Minden (took over Compute North's planned Minden build; no MW published), Fortitude Mining in Aurora (15 MW), AAIM Data Centers in Aurora (operating since about October 2024 on an interruptible basis with Southern, per testimony at https://nebraskalegislature.gov/FloorDocs/109/PDF/Transcripts/Revenue/2025-02-12.pdf), and a 14 MW project Hall County approved in January 2023. I could not tie Site 1 to any of these, so operator, location and start year are null. Do not add the Fortitude Aurora row's capacity to this row; it may be the same load.

site_name: NPPD cryptocurrency mining Operation 2 (operator and location not disclosed)
load_basis: 2025 annual average draw: 135,633,975 kWh posted by NPPD for 'Operation 2' under the LB 526 cryptocurrency disclosure, divided by 8,760 hours.
notes: NPPD's page reports two cryptocurrency mining operations of 1 MW or more under its own jurisdiction for 2025 and names neither. Operation 1 is matched to MARA Kearney by its identical MWh. Operation 2 is unidentified; a possible lead is the BginUSA mining complex planned in York (an NPPD retail town) reported by Flatwater Free Press in 2023, but nothing confirms it. A state senator said in February 2025 that NPPD serves about 250 MW of crypto load in total, which would include wholesale customers such as Southern Public Power District; that is a floor statement, not NPPD data.

operator: Fortitude Mining (Digital Currency Group; spun out of Foundry in January 2025)
serving_utility: Southern Public Power District (wholesale customer of NPPD)
notes: Data Center Dynamics describes a 15 MW Fortitude facility in Aurora that participates in Southwest Power Pool markets, with Aurora supplied by Southern Public Power District under its wholesale agreement with NPPD. The article page returned 403 to a direct fetch, so these details come from the search-result excerpt and the headline only: medium confidence, and the 15 MW is recorded as capacity rather than as 2025 load. Its metered energy is presumably one of Southern's three anonymous LB 526 sites, so load_mw_2025 is null to avoid double counting. Whether this is the same Aurora facility that AAIM Data Centers described to the Legislature in February 2025 is unknown. Fortitude's separate 12 MW Grand Island site only reached commercial readiness in July 2026 (https://decrypt.co/374491) and is outside the 2025 window. No street address found.

Listed because it is very likely above 10 MW, but no load figure was found. The cited article calls Yahoo a large OPPD customer in La Vista that planned to move onto OPPD's dedicated large-load schedule, whose eligibility floor is 20 MW of demand; that implies but does not state a load of 20 MW or more. Whether Yahoo actually moved to that schedule is not confirmed, so the arrangement is unknown. Opening year not sourced in this pass. Yahoo was not among the six data centers named in KOLN's reporting on the 2026 state annual reports. Coordinates are the OSM centroid already in the inventory.

load_basis: Annual average draw: 9,397.6 MWh reported by Travelers in its annual data center report to the Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment, as published by KOLN on 2026-10-29, divided by 8,760 hours. Reporting year taken to be 2025.
notes: Under the 10 MW threshold; included only because it is a known inventory site with a newly reported metered figure, which is about a third of the 3.0 MW the inventory carries from generator permits. KOLN labels it Omaha; the cited article places Travelers' data center in Sarpy County, which matches the inventory coordinates (41.1278, -96.1456), so city is left null. OPPD is inferred from the location being inside OPPD's service area, hence low confidence. The inventory's 2015 start year was not checked.
